propositions: T5c security review currently uses gate-wide AS-WRITTEN evaluative stance, but 46% of strong findings cite repo artifacts and 30% emit template-shape undeclared-access-posture findings, indicating misalignment between posture and exploitability grounding.
The same-round dedup rule emits one finding per undeclared surface; the new rule must cap undeclared-access-posture findings at one per plan with additional surfaces folded into evidence.
Ungrounded findings (those citing neither repo artifacts nor quoted plan text) must be demoted to MINOR severity, not suppressed, while grounded findings retain their strength.
Only two HIGH-class findings warrant severity >= major: plaintext secrets on boundary-crossing paths and undeclared internet-reachable sensitive surfaces; all other findings must be at most minor.

T5c routing must shift from advisory @ 0.95 to blocking @ 0.9, with criterion-local rubric text overriding the shared preamble's evaluate-spec-AS-WRITTEN default to ground evaluation in current codebase and configuration.
